transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, nice to meet you too, Doc. I guess what brings me in is... well, since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I’m up and moving from one little job to the next all day long, exactly like I still have a crew waiting on me to give the orders. 

Speaking of the crew, my old buddy Mike from the site called me the other day. He just bought one of those new electric trucks. Can you believe that? An electric pickup.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?
Less sleep? No, I wouldn't say that. I still get my regular six or seven hours, same as I always did. I'm usually out like a light once my head
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I'm not a worrier. Never have been, really. I just take things as they come, you know? Like when the transmission blew on my old Ford back in '98. Everyone said I should be stressed about how I was gonna get to the job site, but I just figured it out. Traded it in for a Chevy. Best truck I ever owned. Had this deep blue paint job, they called it 'ocean metallic' or something fancy like that. My wife hated the color, said it showed the dirt too much. But she complains about the dirt I track into the house anyway, so what difference did it make? We just got new carpets last year, actually. Cost an arm and a leg.
Do you often lose track of what you were saying because something else catches your attention?

Yeah, I guess I do. It's like... well, if I’m trying to sit down and paint, or maybe plan out a little story, and I hear a truck go by outside, or even just suddenly think of something I need to do in the garden, my mind jumps right over there and I completely lose where I was. The thought is just gone. 

Speaking of
Did you have this same kind of distractibility when you were a child?

Oh, absolutely. Even back in grade school, I remember my teachers telling my folks that I was bright but, you know, just scattered. I was always losing my pencils. Which, actually, reminds me—remember those big, thick yellow pencils they used to give the younger kids? The ones with those huge pink erasers that didn't even erase, they just smeared the graphite all over your paper? God, I hated those things. My buddy Tommy and I used to try and carve our initials into the wooden desks with them. 

But yeah, I was always calling out answers without raising my hand, and the teachers constantly had to remind me to actually finish my work before recess. Recess was the only thing I cared about anyway. We used to play kickball out on this old black
